e.meaning: the outer cup of a flower bud
e.etymology: The botanical word for the ring of sepals that encloses a flower bud, from Greek kalyx, a husk or covering.
A respelling of Iris, the Greek word for rainbow and the goddess who personified it, later the name of the flower.
A Punjabi Sikh name ending in noor, light, a word taken from Arabic.
A recent coinage that reads as lynx, the wild cat, stretched to two syllables, in the style of Lennox and Phoenix.
An English surname from the bird, first a nickname or the trade name of someone who caught and sold finches.
namesakes: Atticus Finch (lawyer hero of To Kill a Mockingbird; surname)

assoc.t: Atticus and Scout Finch, To Kill a Mockingbird

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that builds on Kai with a -ryn ending, close to Kyren and Kieran.
A modern American coinage joining Gray to the -lynn ending, in step with Raelynn and Gracelynn.
From Sanskrit daivika, divine or relating to the gods, from deva, god.
A spelling of Zakai, from Hebrew zakkai, pure or innocent; a Zaccai appears in the Book of Ezra. To American ears it also blends Zak and Kai.
A Yiddish pet form of Leib, lion, a name traditionally paired with Hebrew Aryeh or Yehudah. It is used in Hasidic communities.
An Irish surname, a shortened English form of Ó Lideadha, used as a girls' first name with the feel of Teddy and Lettie.
Arjun, the Sanskrit name of the Mahabharata's archer hero (bright, shining), joined to Reddy, a Telugu family and community name. Arjun Reddy is also a 2017 Telugu hit film.
The scarab-headed Egyptian god of the rising sun, whose name comes from the verb kheper, to come into being.
A recent coinage that sounds like the word heiress and echoes Aries and Paris.
The name of a champion in the video game League of Legends, introduced in 2017 as the partner of Rakan. It has no meaning outside the game.

assoc.t: Xayah, a champion in the game League of Legends

e.etymology: The English word, from Latin luxuria, extravagance or excess.
Known from the rapper Toosii, born Nau'Jour Grainger, who titled his 2023 album Naujour.
A respelling of Amiri, Arabic for princely, from amir, prince or commander. Amiri is also a Los Angeles luxury fashion label often named in hip-hop.

e.meaning: town by the willows or by the stream
e.etymology: An English place name and surname, from Old English welig, willow, or wella, spring or stream, plus tun, settlement.
A spelling of Nicole, the French feminine of Nicholas, from Greek Nikolaos: nike, victory, plus laos, people.
namesakes: Nikole Hannah-Jones (journalist who created The 1619 Project)

e.meaning: great tide, son of the sea
e.etymology: A respelling of Dylan, a Welsh name probably built on words for great and tide. In the Mabinogion, Dylan is a sea-born boy who swims off into the waves.
A variant of William common in Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America. William is Germanic, joining will, desire, and helm, helmet or protection.

e.meaning: fair, blessed (Welsh gwyn); also elf friend
e.etymology: A Welsh name whose ending is gwyn, white, fair or blessed. In English-speaking use it also overlaps with Elwin and Alvin, from Old English names meaning elf friend.
namesakes: E. B. White (Charlotte's Web author, born Elwyn Brooks White)

e.etymology: A respelling of Dominic, from Latin Dominicus, of the Lord, once given to boys born on Sunday. Saint Dominic founded the Dominican order.
The feminine of Spanish Zoilo, from the Greek name Zoilos, built on zoe, life.
e.note: In Spanish it sounds like soy la, I am the, the setup for a long-running family of pun names.

e.etymology: A spelling of Linnea, the Swedish name of the twinflower, Linnaea borealis, named for botanist Carl Linnaeus, whose surname comes from the linden tree.

e.meaning: a name of the god Indra
e.etymology: From Sanskrit Shachindra, lord of Shachi, a title of the god Indra, shortened in Bengali and Marathi. Cricket great Sachin Tendulkar made it famous across India.
From Latin niveus, snowy or snow-white, used in Portuguese as Nívea. US use rose in the early 2000s with the R&B singer Nivea.
e.note: Shares its spelling with the Nivea skin-care brand, which most people will think of first.

e.meaning: descendant of Damhán, a name meaning little stag
e.etymology: A respelling of Devin, from the Irish surname Ó Damháin, descendant of Damhán, a byname built on damh, stag or ox.
A Scottish surname from the town of Livingston in West Lothian, named for a 12th-century landholder called Leving. It has been an occasional American first name since the 1800s.
An Akan day name from Ghana, given to girls born on Saturday; the male counterpart is Kwame.
